description: Statistics Isle of Man published the 2021 Census in two report parts on its census and population page, alongside reports back to 1996 and information on Census 2026. Part II covers the economy, transport and households, with tables for each town, village and parish. Table 3.9 counts households by central heating fuel, with 14,671 on oil, 18,626 on gas and 1,766 on electricity, and table 3.10 counts households with low carbon technology: 794 with a heat pump, 631 with solar panels, 489 with an electric vehicle charging point and 35 with a wind turbine. Other tables give electric vehicle ownership, cars, vans and motorcycles, accommodation type, tenure, bedrooms, and the mode of transport used to get to work or school by area of residence. Coverage is national for the island. Format and access: free PDF reports, no registration. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): OGL (Isle of Man Government Open Government Licence, site-wide). Caveats: the files refuse requests without a browser user agent; tables sit in PDFs. Simulation uses: small-area heat pump and solar adoption, oil heating replacement planning, EV charging demand and commuting mode shares. Related records: none for the Isle of Man in the catalogue.

schema_summary: Part II tables 2.1 to 2.2: employed and school population by area of residence and mode of transport to work or school. Tables 3.1 to 3.18: households by area, size, bedrooms, accommodation type, tenure and rooms; main heating source and central heating fuel (oil, gas, electricity, solid fuel, other) by area; households with a heat pump, passive house system, solar heating, wind turbine, EV charging point or solar panels by area; households with an electric vehicle; cars, vans and motorcycles by area.
